html:
The Umbrella Movement was a 79-day occupation of main roads in Hong Kong, from late September to December 2014, demanding free elections for the city's leader.

In August 2014 China's legislature ruled that candidates for chief executive would have to be screened by a committee loyal to Beijing. Students, led by figures such as Joshua Wong, walked out of classes, and when police fired tear gas, crowds used umbrellas to shield themselves and occupied Admiralty, Mong Kok and Causeway Bay.

The government waited them out and cleared the sites. No reform came. The movement turned many young people toward a local Hong Kong identity, and its leaders were later jailed. Its anger returned on a far larger scale in the protests of 2019, answered by the security law of 2020. It drew on the example of Taiwan's Sunflower movement that spring.
sum: The Umbrella Movement was a 79-day occupation of main roads in Hong Kong, from late September to December 2014, demanding free elections for the city's leader.
